idiom_name: tagged union of node shapes + switch narrowed to never
implementation_notes: The type-level realization of the pattern is a discriminated union: each node shape carries a literal tag, children are arrays of the union itself, and a switch that narrows on the tag (typescriptlang.org's narrowing rules) can be made exhaustive by assigning the default branch to never, turning an unhandled node kind into a compile error. Nodes stay plain data, so the tree is serialisable and structurally comparable, and no class hierarchy is needed. Use the interface/class variant when nodes carry behaviour or are extended by third-party code, where structural typing offers no closed-set guarantee.
pitfalls: The never default only fails the build while type checking runs; a plain JavaScript consumer of the module gets no protection at all.
Structural typing accepts any object literal with the right shape, so data arriving from outside (JSON, storage) must be validated, not asserted.
In DOM trees, childNodes is a NodeList that includes text and comment nodes while children is an element-only HTMLCollection; picking the wrong one silently changes the traversal.

variants.name: Interface/abstract class Component with typed children (extensible nodes)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic translation typechecked: an abstract class (or interface) declares the uniform operation and a container class holds children: Component[], delegating recursively. TypeScript's structural interfaces make uniformity explicit without forcing inheritance, and the DOM typings themselves are this shape - lib.dom.d.ts declares Node, implemented by both Element (containers) and Text (leaves) - so browser code composing elements already uses the pattern. Prefer it when nodes have behaviour, need encapsulation or are extended by other packages; prefer the union variant when the node set is closed and exhaustiveness matters more than openness.
pitfalls: Child management on the Component class makes leaves inherit meaningless add/remove members; keep it on the container and narrow with instanceof.
Arrays are shared by reference, so exposing children directly lets callers corrupt the tree - hand out copies or read-only views.
Recursion over an untrusted or cyclic tree overflows the stack; guard with a visited set or an explicit stack.
